headline: US and Iran sign ceasefire agreement to end war
summary: Presidents Trump and Pezeshkian signed a 14-point interim pact to end hostilities, though Trump warned he would resume attacks if commitments are not honored.
details: US President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian have signed an interim agreement to end their war, marking the first such pact signed by presidents of both nations since 1979.

The 14-point agreement extends a ceasefire for 60 days to allow for negotiations on a permanent truce. It includes an immediate end to the war on all fronts, including Lebanon, and the lifting of a US blockade of Iranian ports.

Key terms include the full resumption of maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, the waiving of US sanctions, the unfreezing of Iranian assets, and a $300 billion investment fund for Iran's post-war reconstruction.
Iran has reaffirmed its vow not to build nuclear weapons and agreed to the 'down-blending' of its enriched uranium stockpile under IAEA supervision.
Despite the agreement, President Trump threatened to 'bomb the hell out of them' if Iran violates the pact, stating he would resume attacks on Iranian officials if commitments are not met.
The conflict, which began on February 28 with the assassination of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has killed over 7,000 people and caused global energy price spikes and food supply concerns.
Trump also recanted his previous vow to destroy Iran's ballistic missile industry, stating it would be 'unfair' for Iran not to have some missiles while other countries do.
caption:
US and Iran end their war with a historic ceasefire agreement, but Trump warns of renewed attacks if the pact is violated.

US President Donald Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian have signed an interim agreement to end their war, marking the first such pact signed by presidents of both nations since 1979.

The 14-point agreement extends a ceasefire for 60 days to allow for negotiations on a permanent truce. It includes an immediate end to the war on all fronts, including Lebanon, and the lifting of a US blockade of Iranian ports.

Key terms include the full resumption of maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, the waiving of US sanctions, the unfreezing of Iranian assets, and a $300 billion investment fund for Iran's post-war reconstruction.

Iran has reaffirmed its vow not to build nuclear weapons and agreed to the 'down-blending' of its enriched uranium stockpile under IAEA supervision.

Despite the agreement, President Trump threatened to 'bomb the hell out of them' if Iran violates the pact, stating he would resume attacks on Iranian officials if commitments are not met.

The conflict, which began on February 28 with the assassination of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has killed over 7,000 people and caused global energy price spikes and food supply concerns.

Trump also recanted his previous vow to destroy Iran's ballistic missile industry, stating it would be 'unfair' for Iran not to have some missiles while other countries do.

headline_marked: Centurions Gill and Kishan [[lead India to series win]] over Afghanistan
headline: Centurions Gill and Kishan lead India to series win over Afghanistan
summary: India secured a massive 170-run victory in Lucknow, sealing the three-match ODI series with two straight wins.
details: Captain Shubman Gill and Ishan Kishan dominated the match with centuries, propelling India to a massive total of 402 after being put in to bat first.
Gill scored 154 off 110 balls, marking his ninth ODI hundred, while Kishan hit an explosive 125 off 79 balls, including seven sixes and 14 boundaries.
The duo added a massive 224-run partnership for the third wicket, punishing the Afghan bowlers through the middle overs.
Afghanistan struggled in pursuit of 403, reaching only 232-9 before the match ended in the 45th over.
Key contributions for Afghanistan included Rahmat Shah's defiant 79 off 89 balls and Sediqullah Atal's 42.
On the bowling side, Gurnoor Brar took 3-60 and Arshdeep Singh claimed 3-45, helping India secure the dominant win.
The victory ensures India wins the three-match ODI series with two consecutive wins.
caption:
A 170-run demolition! Gill and Kishan both hit centuries to crush Afghanistan.

Captain Shubman Gill and Ishan Kishan dominated the match with centuries, propelling India to a massive total of 402 after being put in to bat first.

Gill scored 154 off 110 balls, marking his ninth ODI hundred, while Kishan hit an explosive 125 off 79 balls, including seven sixes and 14 boundaries.

The duo added a massive 224-run partnership for the third wicket, punishing the Afghan bowlers through the middle overs.

Afghanistan struggled in pursuit of 403, reaching only 232-9 before the match ended in the 45th over.

Key contributions for Afghanistan included Rahmat Shah's defiant 79 off 89 balls and Sediqullah Atal's 42.

On the bowling side, Gurnoor Brar took 3-60 and Arshdeep Singh claimed 3-45, helping India secure the dominant win.

The victory ensures India wins the three-match ODI series with two consecutive wins.
